A market analysis for February 2024 revealed a mixed outlook for the dairy industry. While there was some improvement in overall milk prices, Class III futures for February and March were projected to stay below $17/cwt. A significant mitigating factor for producers was the substantial decline in feed costs, with corn and soybean meal futures approaching their contract lows. Furthermore, the U.S. dairy heifer inventory had fallen to its lowest level since 2004, a key detail suggesting that any potential for herd expansion would be significantly constrained.

A mid-January market update, published on January 17, 2025, indicated that Class III and IV milk prices had been trending higher over the preceding month. The report noted that cheese markets had rallied from their early December lows, a trend supported by stronger export activity as the price gap between U.S. and European cheese narrowed. However, the update also cautioned that new production capacity expected to come online in the coming months could temper further price gains.

In the first quarter of 2024, United States molybdenum prices demonstrated remarkable stability, bolstered by robust demand from the steel industry and consistent operations from major producers, including Freeport-McMoRan Inc. and Southern Copper Corp. A notable price increase occurred in February 2024, which was propelled by a significant surge in demand that kept smelters operating at full capacity as steel mills continued to place substantial orders.

A report published on October 7, 2025, revealed that spot prices for molybdenum oxide powder reached their highest level of the year, a surge that commenced in July attributed to a tightening supply of molybdenite concentrate. The Platts assessment for spot prices peaked at $26.025 per pound on September 3, 2025, a significant increase from $21.925 per pound on July 1.

ExxonMobil announced the successful startup of its Beaumont refinery expansion on March 16, 2023. [2, 4, 9] The $2 billion project, which began construction in 2019, added 250,000 barrels per day of crude oil processing capacity, increasing the facility's total capacity to over 630,000 barrels per day and making it one of the largest refineries in the United States. [4, 6, 10] The expansion is designed to process light crude oil from the Permian Basin to produce more transportation fuels such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel, helping to meet growing demand. [4, 5] The primary focus reported by the company and industry news sources was on transportation fuels. [4, 7, 10]

On July 16, 2024, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced nearly $10 million in funding for two projects aimed at lowering the costs and reducing the environmental impact of producing rare earth elements and other critical minerals from coal and its by-products. The projects, awarded under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, will concentrate on advanced laboratory and bench-scale testing to improve the economic viability of separation and refining technologies.

China's Northern Rare Earth Group announced on August 1, 2024, that its listed prices for rare earth products for that month would be unchanged from July 2024. The price for praseodymium-neodymium oxide was held at 384,800 yuan per ton. This decision by a major global supplier had a significant impact on market confidence at the beginning of the month. While prices were stable at the time of the announcement, by the end of August, praseodymium-neodymium oxide prices had increased by 7.5% compared to the beginning of the month.

<3> Projections for the third and fourth quarters of 2024 suggested a potential stabilization in neodymium prices, with multiple commodity research firms anticipating moderate growth. This outlook was largely driven by expanding demand from the green technology sector, particularly for use in electric vehicles and wind turbines. [1] While one source indicated these preliminary projections foresaw moderate growth [1], other analyses from mid-2024 pointed to a surplus of neodymium for the remainder of the year, with market tightness and potential price increases not expected until 2026. [5, 6] Another viewpoint suggested that a market improvement and increased purchasing activity could occur in the fourth quarter of 2024. [5, 6] Forecasts from Argus Media also indicated a future imbalance between supply and demand beginning in 2025, which is expected to lead to price increases. [7]

Market analysts reported that the spot price of Neodymium-Praseodymium (NdPr) surged to $123 per kilogram, officially breaking above the $110 per kilogram price-support threshold. This threshold functions as a strategic downside backstop established in the U.S. Department of Defense's 10-year strategic supply agreement with domestic producer MP Materials. The price rally, which brought NdPr to its highest level since July 2022, was driven by tight supply resulting from China's deliberate management of mining quotas and MP Materials halting incremental concentrate shipments to China.

In January 2023, the London Metal Exchange (LME) released a report from independent consultancy group Oliver Wyman, which reviewed the events that led to a significant nickel price increase and a week-long trading suspension in March 2022. The report concluded that the LME failed to adequately police large positions on the nickel market and lacked sufficient volatility controls to manage the soaring prices. The review recommended that the LME implement stronger risk and control functions, upgrade its volatility controls, and increase its monitoring of market risks to prevent future distortions.
In its April 2023 outlook, the World Bank forecast nickel prices to drop by about 15 percent in 2023 and by another 9 percent in 2024.
In its October 2023 outlook, the World Bank projected the annual average nickel price to fall from $22,350.00 per metric ton in 2023 to $20,000.00 per metric ton in 2024.

In mid-June 2023, London Metal Exchange (LME) nickel futures and spot prices experienced a notable increase, reaching a two-week high. [3] This price rally was primarily driven by macroeconomic factors, including a weakening U.S. dollar, which was influenced by data showing U.S. inflation cooling to its lowest level since March 2021. [2, 3] The cooled inflation data, released on June 13, 2023, led the U.S. Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady, further buoying market sentiment. [3] This price surge occurred despite low fundamental demand for nickel at the time. [2] The LME three-month nickel price rose from $20,755 per metric ton on June 12 to $23,034 per metric ton by June 16, 2023. [3]

In the fourth quarter of 2023, nickel prices experienced a significant decline, with the London Metal Exchange (LME) price falling to as low as $16,000 per tonne late in the year. [1] This downturn was attributed to a combination of factors, primarily a substantial surplus of nickel on the market. [1, 9] A major contributor to this surplus was a surge in the supply of lower-quality nickel pig iron from Indonesia, which now accounts for about half of the global supply. [2, 5] Concurrently, demand from the stainless steel sectors in the United States and Europe was weak. [1, 14] The situation was exacerbated by a record-high number of short positions held by investment funds on the LME, amidst global inflationary pressures and high interest rates. [1] The average LME nickel price for 2023 was $21,474 per tonne, a 16% decrease from the 2022 average. [1]

S&P Global Commodity Insights announced in its June 2023 Nickel Commodity Briefing Service report a downgrade of its average London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month nickel price forecast for the second half of 2023. [1] The forecast was lowered from $22,000 per metric ton to $20,000 per metric ton. [1] This revision was attributed to the expectation that increased primary nickel production in Indonesia and China would outpace the growth in consumption in China. [1] The report noted that the LME three-month nickel closing price had already dropped to a new 2023 low of $20,056 per metric ton on June 28, 2023. [1]

On April 12, 2024, the U.S. and U.K. governments jointly announced new sanctions targeting Russian-origin nickel, aluminum, and copper to curtail Russia's revenue from metal exports. This action prohibited the import of these metals into the U.S. and barred major global exchanges, such as the London Metal Exchange (LME) and Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME), from accepting new Russian-produced supplies. In immediate reaction to the news, nickel futures prices experienced a significant rally on the next trading day, Monday, April 15, 2024. The LME three-month nickel price surged, climbing to a seven-month high of $19,355 per metric ton. This upward trend continued, with prices reaching $19,739 per ton by April 22.

In response to new US and UK sanctions on Russian metals announced on April 12, 2024, nickel prices experienced a significant upward trend. The sanctions targeted Russia's export revenues by prohibiting the import of Russian-origin aluminum, copper, and nickel into the United States and limiting their trade on global exchanges like the London Metal Exchange (LME) and Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME). This action followed an existing UK ban on Russian metal imports from December 2023. Subsequently, on April 19, 2024, the LME nickel futures price surpassed the $19,000 per ton mark, closing at $19,326 per ton. The price rally continued into May, with nickel reaching a year-to-date high of $21,615 per tonne on May 20.

<1> In a report published on January 25, 2024, market analyst Mark Selby of Crux Investor suggested the nickel market was showing signs of bottoming out after a period of price weakness, arguing that the price slide had prompted "the capitulation which heralds a bottom." Selby predicted that a combination of production cuts from major operators and strong, underestimated demand from the electric vehicle (EV) sector could lead to a price surge. He specifically noted that demand from trucks and large EVs in the U.S. was a significant factor, with sales up 50% year-over-year. Citing a potential 30-40% growth in overall EV-related nickel demand for the year, Selby forecasted that prices could rebound to $20,000 per tonne by the end of 2024.

<1> The nickel market entered 2024 with a substantial surplus carried over from 2023, a situation primarily driven by a surge in production from Indonesia and China. This glut includes both lower-purity Class 2 nickel from Indonesia and higher-purity Class 1 from China. [3] The oversupply coincided with weakened demand, notably from China's stainless steel industry, which was affected by a sluggish recovery in the country's construction sector post-COVID lockdowns. [4, 5] This imbalance has exerted significant downward pressure on nickel prices, a trend expected to continue as the global surplus persists. [3, 4]

Nickel prices experienced a significant downward trend during the majority of the fourth quarter of 2024. The price per metric ton reached a peak of $18,221 on October 2 before falling to $15,732 by the end of the month. Following a brief recovery to $16,607 on November 7, prices continued to decline, hitting a 2024 low of $15,090 on December 19. The year concluded with the price at $15,300 on December 31.

On November 12, 2025, the United States Mint struck its final circulating penny, concluding 232 years of production due to rising material costs. With the penny's elimination, the five-cent nickel became the lowest-value U.S. coin in production. This milestone has sparked intense debate over the nickel's viability, as elevated base metal prices have driven its production cost up to nearly 14 cents per coin.

text:
[Source publication date: 2017-03-10.] UK chancellor Philip Hammond announced Philip Hammond's 2017 budget on Wednesday, which included a £2 billion pledge to social care and a tax hike on the self-employed. It was accused of breaking Conservative Party manifesto promises.

It was announced there will be a 2% increase in national insurance contributions for the self-employed, with chancellor Philip Hammond citing worries that people were choosing to become self-employed in order to pay lower taxes and Philip Hammond's perception of unfairness in the different rates paid by employees and self-employees. There were accusations this change in policy goes against the manifesto promises the Conservative Party ran on in 2015, which promised four times that there would be no increase in national insurance rates. Conservative MP Anna Soubry tweeted saying Anna Soubry believed these new measures would be unpopular as many would see them as unfair. The leader of the opposition, Jeremy Corbyn, claimed the new measures will not clamp down on people whose self-employment is just for tax benefits, instead causing problems for those legitimately self-employed, arguing that if they are to start paying similar tax rates to the employed then they should get rights such as statutory maternity pay. The think tank Resolution claimed, however, this increase is outweighed by other government policies and is, therefore, a good move.

In addition to this, the chancellor announced a £2 billion pledge to social care over the next three years, saying Philip Hammond was aware of the stress the ageing population is having on the NHS and social care. Liberal Democrat Norman Lamb described the amount as "wholly inadequate", saying much more is needed to pay for an increase in care demands due to the ageing population. The lowest threshold at which shareholders pay dividend taxes is to be lowered from £5,000 to £2,000 claiming that the taxes for dividends provided "an extremely generous tax break for investors with substantial share portfolios". Other budget announcements include an additional £325 million for the NHS, £90 million transport spending for the North of England, £20 million to support campaigning against violence against girls and women and a slight increase in funding for the devolved governments.

text:
[Source publication date: 2017-07-15.] On Wednesday, three-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic withdrew from this year's tournament suffering from an elbow injury. The announcement was made after the Serbian took a medical timeout during the second set in the quarter-final against Czech tennis player Tomáš Berdych.

Djokovic said, "It's unfortunate that I had to finish Wimbledon, a grand slam, this way [...] I mean, if someone feels bad about it, it's me. But, you know, I tried." Novak Djokovic's elbow was problematic for more than a year, Novak Djokovic said. Novak Djokovic also said, "I was able for 30 minutes to play with pain that was bearable. The serve and forehand were the shots where I could feel it the most and after that there was really no sense".

Djokovic's pre-quarterfinal against Adrian Mannarino was rescheduled to Tuesday, so the 30-year-old Serbian had to play two matches in two days. Djokovic was two sets down with the scoreboard 7–6 2–0 when world number-two Djokovic decided to stop despite leading their head-to-head record, 25–2.

31-year-old Berdych therefore advanced to play the semi-final against Swiss seven-time Wimbledon Singles Champion Roger Federer. Berdych's best record at the Wimbledon was finalist in 2010, against Rafa Nadal — when Tomáš Berdych defeated Federer in quarterfinal. The Czech has never won a Grand Slam title.

target_variable: Roy Hodgson [English Wikipedia daily pageviews; total_all_access]
text:
[Source publication date: 2017-09-15.] On Tuesday, former manager of England's football team Roy Hodgson signed a two-year contract with London-based football club Crystal Palace, the club announced via their official website.

70-year-old Hodgson has about forty years as a football manager, and has managed fifteen clubs, and four countries' national teams. Roy Hodgson has managed four Premier League clubs — Blackburn Rovers, Fulham FC, Liverpool and West Bromwich, having 34.72 % win rate in Premier League. In 2011, Roy Hodgson helped West Bromwich avoid relegation, and a year earlier, Roy Hodgson helped Fulham to reach the final of the UEFA Europa League. Hodgson went on to manage England. Under Roy Hodgson's management, The Three Lions reached the quarter-finals of the UEFA Euro 2012. In 2014's FIFA World Cup, England were eliminated in the group stage, and last year, following 2–1 defeat against Iceland in Euro 2016, Roy Hodgson announced resignation from the post. Hodgson has won seven Swedish league titles, two Swedish cups, and one league title each in Switzerland and Denmark.

After penning the deal, Hodgson said, "This is very much the club of my boyhood and I remember in my youth watching the club from the terraces at the Holmesdale Road end which gave me such fond memories. In those days I had dreams of playing for the team, then as a coach you think about coaching the team and a lot has happened in between times." Regarding the poor start of the season, Hodgson said, "I don't honestly believe that there is necessarily a lot that needs to be done. You can always get off to a bad start, what we've got to remember is our fate will be decided after 38 games, not four."

Hodgson's predecessor Frank de Boer's three-year contract was terminated the day before Hodgson's hiring, after Roy Hodgson's fourth consecutive defeat in the English Premier League. Crystal Palace was yet to score a goal, and they were nineteenth in the league table. Hodgson is now the oldest permanent manager in the Premier League. Roy Hodgson is also the seventh manager of Crystal Palace in the past six years.

Hodgson's first match as Crystal Palace's manager is to be an away match against Southampton FC, scheduled for tomorrow.

[Source publication date: 2017-09-15.] This morning local time an explosion, now officially considered a terrorist incident, was reported on a London underground train which was stopped at Parsons Green in south-west London. The explosion has been officially confirmed caused by an improvised device placed in a white bucket inside a Lidl shopping bag. Reports also indicate a timer attached to the explosive. At least 29 people were injured, NHS England said this afternoon.

Officers and ambulance staff were on the scene this morning, with reports of burn and crush injuries. Detectives and MI5 were investigating.

BBC News presenter Sophie Raworth described seeing a woman on a stretcher with face and leg burns.

In a statement after the incident, British Prime Minister Theresa May said, "My thoughts are with those injured at Parsons Green and emergency services who are responding bravely to this terrorist incident."
